section.heading: Application for a protection zone installation permit

content.p: (1) A carrier may apply to the ACMA for a permit (a protection zone installation permit) to:
install one or more submarine cables in a protection zone; or
install a single international submarine cable in both:
a protection zone; and
Australian waters that are not in a protection zone and that are not coastal waters of a State or the Northern Territory; or

a protection zone; and
Australian waters that are not in a protection zone and that are not coastal waters of a State or the Northern Territory.

section.heading: Matters to which the ACMA must have regard in making a decision about a permit

content.p: In deciding whether to grant a protection zone installation permit, the ACMA must have regard to:
if the Secretary of the Attorney-General’s Department makes a submission to the ACMA under clause 55A—that submission; and
any other matters that the ACMA considers relevant.

If the Attorney-General, after consulting the Prime Minister and the Minister administering this Act, considers that the grant of a protection zone installation permit to a particular carrier would be prejudicial to security, the Attorney-General may give a written direction to the ACMA not to grant a protection zone installation permit to the carrier.
The ACMA must comply with a direction under subclause (1).
While a direction is in force under this clause:
the ACMA cannot reconsider a non-compulsory refusal to grant a protection zone installation permit to the carrier; and
the Administrative Appeals Tribunal cannot consider an application for review of a non-compulsory refusal to grant a protection zone installation permit to the carrier.
If an application for a protection zone installation permit is pending at the time when the Attorney-General gives a direction to the ACMA under this clause, then the application lapses.
In this clause:
non-compulsory refusal means a refusal to grant a protection zone installation permit, other than a refusal that is required by this clause.
Further information requested
If:
a carrier applies for a protection zone installation permit; and
the ACMA requests the applicant to give the ACMA further information under subclause 55(1) in relation to the application;
the ACMA must take all reasonable steps to ensure that a decision is made on the application within:
25 business days; or
if the ACMA, by written notice given to the applicant, specifies a greater number of business days (not exceeding 35 business days)—that number of business days;
after the day on which the applicant gave the ACMA the information.
No further information requested

a carrier applies for a protection zone installation permit; and
the ACMA does not request the applicant to give the ACMA further information under subclause 55(1) in relation to the application;

25 business days; or

after the day on which the application was made.

a carrier applies for a protection zone installation permit; and
the carrier notifies the ACMA of a change in circumstances under subclause 54A(1); and
the ACMA decides under subclause 54A(2) that the change should not be treated as a material change in circumstances for the purposes of this clause;
the number of business days referred to in subclause (1) or (2) of this clause is extended by 5 business days.
If:

If the Attorney-General, after consulting the Prime Minister and the Minister administering this Act, considers that the grant of a non-protection zone installation permit to a particular carrier would be prejudicial to security, the Attorney-General may give a written direction to the ACMA not to grant a non-protection zone installation permit to the carrier.
The ACMA must comply with a direction under subclause (1).
While a direction is in force under this clause:
the ACMA cannot reconsider a non-compulsory refusal to grant a non-protection zone installation permit to the carrier; and
the Administrative Appeals Tribunal cannot consider an application for review of a non-compulsory refusal to grant a non-protection zone installation permit to the carrier.
If an application for a non-protection zone installation permit is pending at the time when the Attorney-General gives a direction to the ACMA under this clause, then the application lapses.
In this clause:
non-compulsory refusal means a refusal to grant a non-protection zone installation permit, other than a refusal that is required by this clause.
Further information requested
If:
a carrier applies for a non-protection zone installation permit; and
the ACMA requests the applicant to give the ACMA further information under subclause 68(1) in relation to the application;
the ACMA must take all reasonable steps to ensure that a decision is made on the application within:
60 business days; or
if the ACMA, by written notice given to the applicant, specifies a greater number of business days (not exceeding 90 business days)—that number of business days;
after the day on which the applicant gave the ACMA the information.
No further information requested
If:
a carrier applies for a non-protection zone installation permit; and
the ACMA does not request the applicant to give the ACMA further information under subclause 68(1) in relation to the application;
the ACMA must take all reasonable steps to ensure that a decision is made on the application within:
60 business days; or
if the ACMA, by written notice given to the applicant, specifies a greater number of business days (not exceeding 90 business days)—that number of business days;
after the day on which the application was made.
Extension for change in circumstances relating to application
If:
a carrier applies for a non-protection zone installation permit; and
the carrier notifies the ACMA of a change in circumstances under subclause 67A(1); and
the ACMA decides under subclause 67A(2) that the change should not be treated as a material change in circumstances for the purposes of this clause;
the number of business days referred to in subclause (1) or (2) of this clause is extended by 5 business days.
If:
a carrier applies for a non-protection zone installation permit; and
the carrier notifies the ACMA of a change in circumstances under subclause 67A(1); and
the ACMA decides under subclause 67A(2) that the change should be treated as a material change in circumstances for the purposes of this clause;
the number of business days referred to in subclause (1) or (2) of this clause is extended by:
60 business days; or
if the ACMA, by written notice given to the applicant, specifies a greater number of business days (not exceeding 90 business days)—that number of business days.
Extension where notice given by Secretary of the Attorney-General’s Department in force
If:
a carrier applies for a non-protection zone installation permit; and
the Secretary of the Attorney-General’s Department gives a notice to the ACMA under paragraph 70(3)(a) of this Schedule in relation to the application;
the number of business days referred to in subclause (1) or (2) of this clause is extended by one business day for each business day in the period during which the notice remains in force.
Insert:
A non-protection zone installation permit held by a carrier is subject to the following conditions:
a condition that the relevant cable or cables must be installed within:
926 metres of the route or routes specified by the ACMA in the permit; or
if the ACMA specifies another distance in the permit—that distance of the route or routes specified by the ACMA in the permit;

a condition that the carrier, or a person acting on behalf of the carrier, must not install the relevant cable or cables unless all Commonwealth regulatory approvals have been obtained for the installation;
such conditions (if any) in relation to security as the ACMA specifies in the permit;
such conditions (if any) in relation to the installation of the relevant cable or cables as the ACMA specifies in the permit.
Variation of conditions
The ACMA may, by written notice given to the holder of a non-protection zone installation permit:
vary a condition covered by paragraph (1)(a) by:
specifying a distance; or
varying a distance; or
vary a condition covered by paragraph (1)(c) or (d).

content.p: Add:

section.heading: Attorney-General’s consent required for certain enforcement proceedings

content.p: An application for an injunction under section 564 must not be made without the written consent of the Attorney-General if:
the injunction is in relation to a contravention by a carrier of the carrier licence condition set out in Part 1 of Schedule 1 in so far as that condition relates to this Division; and
the carrier is a foreign national; and
the contravention occurred, is occurring, or is to occur, outside Australia; and
the contravention did not involve an Australian ship.
A proceeding for the recovery of a pecuniary penalty under section 571 must not be instituted without the written consent of the Attorney-General if:
the proceeding is in respect of a contravention by a carrier of the carrier licence condition set out in Part 1 of Schedule 1 in so far as that condition relates to this Division; and
the carrier is a foreign national; and
the contravention occurred outside Australia; and
the contravention did not involve an Australian ship.

In deciding whether to consent under subclause (1) or (2), the Attorney-General must have regard to the obligations of Australia under international law, including obligations under any agreement between:
Australia; and
another country or countries.

section.heading: Installing an international submarine cable without a permit

content.p: Omit “a submarine cable”, substitute “an international submarine cable”.

section.heading: Installing a domestic submarine cable without a permit

content.p: A person commits an offence if:
the person installs, or causes to be installed, a domestic submarine cable; and
the cable is installed in a protection zone; and
the person does not have a permit under this Part authorising the installation of the cable in the place in which it is installed.
Penalty: 200 penalty units.
Strict liability applies to paragraph (1)(b).
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
Subclause (1) does not apply to a person who installs a domestic submarine cable on behalf of a carrier, if the carrier has a permit authorising the installation of the cable.
Note: The defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subclause (3). See subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
Subclause (1) does not apply to a domestic submarine cable that a person installed, or began to install, before the commencement of this clause.
Note: The defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matters in subclause (4). See subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
Before “A carrier”, insert “(1)”.

section.heading: Failing to comply with ACMA direction to remove an unlawfully installed domestic submarine cable

content.p: The ACMA may direct a carrier to remove a domestic submarine cable if:
the carrier installed the submarine cable, or caused it to be installed, in a protection zone without a permit under this Part authorising the installation; or
the carrier is installing the submarine cable, or causing it to be installed, in a protection zone without a permit under this Part authorising the installation.
A carrier who does not comply with a direction under subclause (1) commits an offence.
Penalty: 200 penalty units.
The ACMA must not give a direction to a carrier under subclause (1) in relation to a domestic submarine cable that the carrier installed, or began to install, before the commencement of this clause.

content.p: This item applies to a declaration of a protection zone if:

the activity consists of the maintenance or repair of the submarine cable.

content.p: This item applies to a declaration of a protection zone if:
the declaration was in force immediately before the commencement of this item; and

Those restrictions do not apply to an activity if:
the activity is carried on by, or on behalf of, a person who owns or operates a submarine cable in the protection zone; and

content.p: (1) Despite the repeal of clause 32 of Schedule 3A to the Telecommunications Act 1997 by this Schedule, that clause continues to apply, after the commencement of this item, in relation to a proposal developed under clause 30 of Schedule 3A to the Telecommunications Act 1997 before the commencement of this item, as if that repeal had not happened.

a decision to grant or to refuse to grant a protection zone installation permit if the application for the permit was made after the commencement of this item.

The amendments of Division 3 of Part 3 of Schedule 3A to the Telecommunications Act 1997 by this Schedule (other than amendments relating to the conditions of a non-protection zone installation permit) apply in relation to:
